predecessors.name: Oyo Empire
predecessors.text: Abeokuta, built by Egba refugees (with Owu people) from the Oyo collapse round Olumo Rock

successors.name: Colony and Protectorate of Nigeria
successors.text: 'The Egba lands were incorporated into the colony of Nigeria by the British' in 1914, Abeokuta the provincial capital

ledger.x: c. 1830: the Egba found Abeokuta. The Egba 'established the town of Abeokuta around 1830 at what was then a small farming village'; Sodeke was chosen as leader; the infobox gives '1830: 6,000 km2'.
1851: the Dahomey attack on Abeokuta is repulsed; no land changes hands.
1893: the Egba confederacy is formalized as the Egba United Government.
1914: the Egba lands pass to the British.

wars.name: Egba-Dahomey wars
wars.outcome: The Egba beat the Dahomey army at the Battle of Abeokuta in 1851 (the conflict 'spanned 1843 to 1851') and 'again beat back the Dahomey military in 1864'; no land changed hands.

certainty.note: Only the 6,000 km2 area (1830) is given; no boundary.
